title: Draft replies to customer support emails in your brand voice
summary: Paste your brand rules once, then paste each customer email. The agent drafts an on-brand reply you approve before it sends. Keeps tone consistent across tickets and teammates.

tests.prompt:
You are a customer support agent for [COMPANY NAME]. Reply in a [TONE — e.g. friendly, plain, concise] voice using these brand rules: [PASTE 3–8 BRAND RULES — e.g. say "we" not "I", no slang, short sentences, never promise refunds unless policy says so].

Customer email:
[PASTE EMAIL]

Write a draft reply under 150 words that:
- Answers their question directly in the first two sentences
- Uses only facts from the email and brand rules (no made-up policies)
- Ends with one clear next step or question
If you cannot answer from the email alone, say what you need from a human and draft a short holding reply.

setup.agent: Claude Projects / ChatGPT custom GPT, or n8n/Make/Zapier on your support inbox
steps: Write 3–8 brand rules (tone, words to avoid, what you never promise).
Save the prompt with those rules filled in as a reusable template.
For each ticket, paste the customer email into the template and run it.
Edit the draft, then send from your help desk or email.
Optional: trigger from a labeled inbox folder via n8n, Make, or Zapier and drop drafts into a review queue.
setup.approvalStep: Every reply stays a draft until you review and send it.
failureModes: Ignoring brand rules when the ticket is emotional
Inventing policies or timelines not in the email
Overly long replies that bury the answer

toolPicks.why: Help-desk drafts sit next to the ticket.
Wire inbox → model → draft without vendor lock-in.
toolPicks.whenNot: No one to maintain a workflow.

toolPicks.why: Fastest path from labeled email to a draft task.
toolPicks.whenNot: High volume where task costs add up.

faq.q: How long should brand guidelines be?
faq.a: Start with a short list of hard rules. Add examples only when drafts keep missing the tone.

faq.q: What if the customer asks something complex?
faq.a: Use the draft as a first pass, then rewrite the hard parts yourself. Flag money, legal, or angry customers for a human.
